subject: Post-demo: egress hop budgeting + private deploy runbook
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@nebula-analytics.com>; Priya Sinha <priya@nebula-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 22 Aug 2027 14:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-demo: quick recap and targeted SLOs for private deploy

Thanks again for the call earlier — good visibility into Nebula's streaming use case and expected load. Summary and concrete asks below so we can converge on a pre-production validation plan.

High-level targets (what we discussed / what Redwood will design for):
- Streaming initial-chunk latency (end-to-end): <= 150 ms p95
- Token tail latency (single-token decode once streaming started): <= 35 ms p95
- Sustained aggregate throughput: ~10k tokens/s across the cluster (you estimated ~7–9k steady; plan headroom to 10k)
- Concurrent streaming sessions: 250 baseline, scale-to 500 for burst tests
- KV-cache concurrency: support for 1k concurrent cached sessions during peak

Network / private deploy constraints we need to validate:
- VPC peering / VPN path RTT budget: <= 40 ms RTT between Nebula app subnet and the Redwood inference subnet for gold path
- Acceptable jitter: < 10 ms (otherwise token jitter can cause visible frame gaps in streaming UIs)
- Egress bandwidth baseline: 1 Gbps is minimum; recommend 5 Gbps to avoid TCP queuing during bursts
- MTU: 1500 preferred; note if you use jumbo frames we need to coordinate MTU and path MTU discovery
- NAT egress concurrent mappings: ensure NAT devices support ~2k concurrent ephemeral ports for sessions + health checks

Immediate asks for Nebula:
1) Attach traceroute and a ping histogram from a representative app host to the three Redwood endpoints we discussed (we provided DNS names on the call).
2) Run an iperf3 bi-directional test to one of our endpoints for 5 minutes (ideally during an off-peak window) and share a CSV of the results.
3) If feasible, run a short TCP streaming test from your app host that sends WebSocket-style framed payloads at 50 rps for 10 minutes so we can measure real-world jitter and reassembly behavior.

What Redwood will deliver by Wed (08/25):
- A one-page runbook for the NetOps team with exact iperf/traceroute commands and an automated script pack (egress-test-scripts.tar.gz).
- A private-deploy SLO proposal (minimum acceptance criteria + recommended headroom)
- A short checklist for firewall rules, keepalives, and NAT timeout settings we need you to verify

Next step: can you confirm a 30–60 min window on Tue 08/24 to run the tests? If you prefer Wed morning we can accommodate.

Thanks,
Marcus
Marcus Lin
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
+1 (415) 555-0198

Attachment stubs referenced: nebula-traceroute-to-redwood.txt (please attach your traceroute output), egress-test-scripts.tar.gz (Redwood will upload)
From: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@nebula-analytics.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Sinha <priya@nebula-analytics.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 09:06:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-demo: quick recap and targeted SLOs for private deploy

Appreciate the clear list, Marcus. We're aligned on the targets in principle — a couple clarifications before we run the tests:
- We can schedule the iperf3/test window Tue 08/24 10:00–10:30 PT. That works for our infra team.
- Baseline egress: we can provision a 5 Gbps path for the test window, but want to confirm your expected traffic profile during the test (peak concurrent connections and per-connection throughput) so we can size NAT gateway and retention.

I've attached the initial traceroute from our prod-app-1 host to the primary Redwood endpoint (nebula-traceroute-to-redwood.txt). You can see two ISP hops in the middle — average RTT to us is ~22–28 ms on that path.

Quick answers:
- We'll run the WebSocket-style streaming at 60 rps for a 10-minute window. Each message payload will be ~1–1.5 KB (JSON delta updates); expect ~700–900 tokens per second per 60 rps burst across our aggregate test runner (we'll provide a sampling of the payloads).
- NAT ephemeral port capacity: our current gateway supports ~4k concurrent ephemeral ports, so we should be OK for the stated concurrency.

Attaching: nebula-traceroute-to-redwood.txt (truncated stub).

Sanjay Rao
Head of Infrastructure | Nebula Analytics
sanjay.rao@nebula-analytics.com

Attachment: nebula-traceroute-to-redwood.txt (see full file attached to this thread)
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 23 Aug 2027 11:41:00 -0700
Subject: Internal: prepping runbook and scripts for Nebula test window (08/24)

Karthik / Vanessa — quick internal coordination. Sanjay confirmed Tue 10:00–10:30 PT test window and attached traceroute. Action items:
- Karthik: can you finalize the iperf3 server config + port list and drop the iperf3 command lines into egress-test-scripts.tar.gz? Include --log-like CSV and bi-directional testing flags. Also include an example netcat/WebSocket payload replayer for their 60 rps test.
- Vanessa: please assemble the short SLO proposal PDF (one page) that lists acceptance gates (network RTT, jitter, packet loss, MTU, NAT mappings) and the recommended headroom (we recommended 20% headroom on bandwidth). Call out the fallback policy: if p95 initial-chunk > 200 ms during test we move to warm-cache-only plan and schedule deeper debugging.
- I'll prepare the firewall rule checklist and the HubSpot update (deal RD-2027-045) with the test artifacts link.

Target to you both: have the scripts + PDF into the shared Drive folder by EOD Mon so I can send to Nebula first thing Tue morning.

Thanks — Marcus
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Sanjay Rao <sanjay.rao@nebula-analytics.com>; Priya Sinha <priya@nebula-analytics.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwood.ai>, Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 24 Aug 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Runbook + SLO proposal for Tue test window (links + next steps)

Sanjay / Priya — thanks again for aligning on the window. Links and attachments below: 
- Runbook & scripts (egress-test-scripts.tar.gz): https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3c-example-runbook (contains iperf3 CSV templates, netcat replayer, tcpdump sampling command).
- SLO proposal (redwood-private-slo-proposal.pdf): attached. High-level acceptance gates from the PDF:
  * p95 initial-chunk latency <= 150 ms
  * p95 token tail latency <= 35 ms
  * sustained aggregate throughput >= 8k tokens/s for the test window (we'll accept >=8k as a pass for baseline)
  * jitter < 10 ms and packet loss < 0.1%

Test plan: start with iperf3 bi-directional for 5 minutes, then run the 10-minute 60 rps streaming replay (we'll collect tcpdump samples and token latencies on our side). Please upload the iperf3 CSV and the streaming logs to the shared Drive when done.

If the SLO gates fail during the test we'll do the following:
1) capture a 1-minute pcap and annotate timestamps
2) isolate whether the issue is egress bandwidth, NAT exhaustion, or an intermediate-hop spike
3) if RTT spikes > 200 ms for p95, switch to warm-cache-only route and schedule a deeper network triage with both network teams.

I'll update the HubSpot deal with test artifacts link: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890 and tag the test outcome. Looking forward to the run.

Best,
Marcus
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
marcus.lin@redwood.ai
